answer: Proposal: random live audits in coincident windows. The beacon draws identities for interactive sessions with tight deadlines one machine serves once; a farm cannot forge a second session without a second live machine. A grove of N clone keys on M boxes passes at most M per window, and the odds of in-window colliding rise steeply with headcount, so the fleet buys hardware near headcount or lets keys lapse. Per-key cost stays near linear while reward per key is bounded -- no fable of free scale. Assumes un-delegatable sessions and honest scheduling; rented burst hardware blunts it.
